title: Terminal error payloads: retryable flag and recovery narrative on every error
description: Context: a 2h47m dabble-employee-app agent session made 300 CLI calls with 24 failures. Failure clusters: 117 read-only work show polls (~40% of all calls), 14 identical failed sync refresh retries, 6 vault init retries, 66 agent finish calls with only 2 standalone evidence records, 6 NOT_FOUND finish/release (ownership confusion), 1 CONFLICT claim, 2 POLICY_VIOLATION sprint closes. Design principle for this mission: every response (success or error) must carry enough state that the correct next action is derivable without another read, and the honest path (evidence, ownership, health) must be the path of least resistance. Problem: agents cannot tell dead ends from transient faults. In the audited session, 6 NOT_FOUND finish/release errors and 14 sync failures were all retried because the error gave no signal. Change: every structured CLI/MCP error gains retryable:true|false and a recovery object (what happened, who/what changed the state if known from the ledger, exact next command or none). Example: agent finish on already-closed work must say which agent closed it, when, and retryable:false with no action needed. Where: the error construction path in packages/engine/src/runtime.ts and error rendering in apps/cli/src/commands.ts; enumerate existing BOREAL_* error codes and classify each as retryable or terminal. Constraint: classification table should live in one module (suggest packages/core) so CLI and MCP stay consistent.
acceptanceCriteria: All BOREAL_* error codes carry retryable and recovery fields in --json output
agent finish on closed work names the closing agent and timestamp from the ledger
Classification lives in a single shared module used by both CLI and MCP
